newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: RULING CZECH ODS READY TO DISCUSS CABINET CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: RULING CZECH ODS READY TO DISCUSS CABINET CHANGES.

text.p: The leadership of Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) have agreed to discuss a shakeup in the cabinet with partners in the ruling coalition, Klaus told Czech Radio on Tuesday.
"(The leadership) expressed its agreement with the opening of debate on the reconstruction of the government also with our coalition partners," Klaus said in an interview.

Klaus's government has come under fire in recent weeks for a slowdown in the country's economic performance and for highly publicised cases of financial crime, and problems in the health care sector and schools.

Opinion polls have shown that support for Klaus's centre-right ODS is at a record low while support for the opposition Social Democrats has grown well above that of the three parties in the ruling coalition.

Opposition leaders and some deputies in the ruling coalition have called for the sacking of key ministers including Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik of ODS and Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy of the junior Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA).
The Czech news agency CTK quoted ODS deputy chairman Miroslav Macek as saying that the cabinet should be shuffled by the end of June.
